purpose: Close role-critical gaps between signature-like request detection and evidence-bounded behavioral observation.
principles: A host-specific baseline is scoped evidence, not a universal normal.
Method/status distribution changes can indicate deployment, client mix, crawler, proxy, outage or abuse; preserve alternatives.
A 200 response to a suspicious-looking path proves only the logged status, not that a secret existed or was disclosed.
A 401/403/404 is an application outcome, not proof of malicious intent.
A 5xx rise is operational evidence first; correlate upstream, listener, route and resource evidence before security attribution.
Repeated recurrence across days is persistence evidence, not independent corroboration of actor identity.
Proxy/CDN/NAT/container addresses must be interpreted at the observation boundary before actor attribution.
Traffic volume and confidence alone must not promote authority or certainty.
Partial-day traffic must not be compared as if it were a complete day without rate/time normalization.
Missing telemetry is a blind spot, not negative evidence.
visibility_blind_spots: No request bodies, credentials, tokens or query values are retained.
Response content/body disclosure is not observed from current normalized request ledger.
DNS, TLS handshake/certificate behavior and outbound/egress behavior are not evidence unless an explicit observer is enabled.
Application identity/session semantics are incomplete unless emitted by a dedicated sanitized observer.
Public reachability cannot be inferred from broad local bind alone.
behavioral_learning: Learn host-scoped method and status distributions from historical traffic.
Record distribution shifts as UNUSUAL_UNCERTAIN in shadow mode before alerting.
Use pattern memory state transitions and recurrence as learning progress.
Keep learned experience scoped by host/pattern/source and preserve decay.
